clue.text: It's unlawful to cancel, if one firm goes bust

indicators.note: something that goes bust breaks apart, so the letters of the words before it are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone warns that cancelling a deal would be illegal if a company collapses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes bust' rearranges the fifteen letters of CANCEL IF ONE FIRM; 'to' just links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A breach of the criminal law is by definition something forbidden, so the phrase stands for an unlawful act.

clue.text: Deceptions practised by the light-fingered?

parts.note: light-fingered suggests pickpockets, but here it means the deft hands of a stage magician performing sleight of hand

explanation.definitionFit: Stage illusions done by sleight of hand are deceptions worked by nimble fingers.

clue.text: Gold, perhaps, for leaders of industry not getting other treats

indicators.note: the leaders of a group of words are their opening letters, one from each

explanation.surface: Bosses are offered gold instead of the usual perks.
explanation.definitionFit: A cast bar of metal, of which gold is the classic example, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Exercises sixth sense when homebirds embrace upstart

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold something within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: birds at home: IN (at home) plus TITS (small birds)
the start of the word up, its first letter

explanation.surface: People who stay in welcome a newcomer and sense things by instinct.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'homebirds' as home + birds: IN TITS. 'upstart' is the start of up, U, which 'embrace' puts inside TITS.
explanation.definitionFit: To know by instinct rather than reasoning is to use a sixth sense.

clue.text: A change of attire for a little air

indicators.note: a change of the word attire means its letters are swapped into a new order

explanation.surface: A new outfit is just what's needed for a short tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' links the wordplay to the definition; the surface's change of clothes is really the anagram signal 'change of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A short song or aria in an opera is called by this diminutive musical term.

clue.text: Wild ass brought up to love herb

parts.note: love means nil in tennis scoring, written as the letter O

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing a word up means reading it from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: an onager is a wild ass of Asia

explanation.surface: A wild donkey is raised to adore a culinary plant.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'brought up' reads the wild ass from the bottom upward; 'to' simply joins it to love.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mediterranean culinary plant, wild marjoram, used to season pizza and pasta.

clue.text: Fraud gets round a scavenger

indicators.note: getting round something means surrounding it, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a forger is a fraud who fakes documents or art

explanation.surface: A cheat circles someone who picks through rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: One who searches about for food or provisions is a scavenger of sorts.

clue.text: Neutraliser is ineffective, providing that is right

parts.note: null means void, without effect
providing in the sense of on condition that, if
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A counteracting agent is useless, as long as that is correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that cancels out or voids an effect neutralises it.

clue.text: Heartbroken squeal about milliner is momentous

parts.note: read as heart broken: the letters of heart rearranged

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: to squeal is to inform on someone, as is to sing in slang
a milliner makes hats, a hatter

explanation.surface: A heartbroken cry about a hat-maker turns out to be of great importance.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'Heartbroken' into heart + broken, an anagram of heart. Squeal and sing are both slang for informing to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Something so important it seems to shake the world is momentous.

clue.text: Insomniacs' distraction?

parts.note: the sleepless might fill their wakeful hours with the clubs and bars that are open after dark

explanation.definitionFit: Entertainment in the late hours could amuse those unable to sleep.

clue.text: Governor left with the Queen after the game

indicators.note: after places the pieces before it to follow the game

parts.note: RU is rugby union, the game
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A governor departed with the monarch once the match was over.
explanation.definitionFit: One who rules or governs a land is its sovereign or leader.

clue.text: Peacemakers get Oliver to turn the other way

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, sends peacekeepers
Oliver Twist is Dickens's orphan hero

explanation.surface: Diplomats persuade a famous orphan to change direction.
explanation.definitionFit: To unwind is to rotate in the opposite direction to a twist.

clue.text: Suffering caused by initial loss of flag

indicators.note: losing the initial means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: to flag is to tire or weaken, to languish

explanation.surface: Grief results when the banner is first lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' looks like a banner but is the verb, to weaken.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe mental or physical pain, anguish is acute suffering.

clue.text: A fool about money

indicators.note: turned about means reversed, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a nit is a fool, short for nitwit

explanation.surface: A fool is said to be all about cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Tin is old slang for money, cash.

clue.text: Nourishment discovered in a leading establishment

indicators.note: discovered in means found within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Food was found in a top restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingesta is the technical term for food and drink taken into the body.

clue.text: With a little music, I trilled about my being raised in a German school

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising means turning everything upwards, so the whole run is reversed
a little of the word music means only its opening part is kept
about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to trill is to sing, past tense sang

explanation.surface: Someone recalls singing a little tune while growing up at a school in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a little' keeps just the opening of music; 'about' wraps the sung word round my, and 'being raised' turns the whole run upward in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: In Germany a gymnasium is a secondary school preparing pupils for university.

clue.text: Intended for duck as well

parts.note: to as in addressed to, intended for someone
a duck is a nought in cricket, the letter O

explanation.surface: A duck is meant for someone too.
explanation.definitionFit: Too means also, in addition, as well.

clue.text: GI's hero makes like a man-eater

indicators.note: makes in the sense of forms, so the letters are made into something new

parts.note: the letters of GI's, with the possessive s kept as a letter

explanation.surface: An American soldier's champion behaves like a cannibal.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a giant that eats people, so ogreish behaviour is monstrous.

clue.text: Incoming nurse is a strange creature

annotationWithheld.why: Incoming nurse is a strange creature (3): the answer is hidden in incominG NUrse, but no word but 'Incoming' itself can signal the hidden word, so it does two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Incoming nurse is a strange creature

clue.text: Sweet face's back before the fall

indicators.note: before places the first piece ahead of the second
a face's back is the face read backwards

parts.note: mug is slang for face
a drop is a fall

explanation.surface: A sweet face's last expression before a tumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A chewy gelatine sweet is a type of confection.

clue.text: English can be discovered in French street following …

indicators.note: to be discovered in something is to be found within it, so pieces go inside

parts.note: rue is French for street
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: An Englishman could be found in a street in France.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs into the next clue; 'following' is a noun here, a band of followers.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue is the following, the band of attendants, of an important person.

clue.text: … scrutiny of girl from South America

indicators.note: from places the girl as coming out of, after, the country

parts.note: Peru is a country of South America
Sal is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Checking up on a young woman from South America.
explanation.definitionFit: A careful reading or examination, a perusal is scrutiny of a text.

clue.text: Aquatic animal has to trap sea monster: boy missing

indicators.note: to trap is to hold inside, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: must means has to

indicators.note: missing means the boy's name is taken away

parts.note: the kraken is a legendary sea monster
Ken is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A water creature must catch a sea monster though the boy is lost.
explanation.walkthrough: KRAKEN minus KEN leaves KRA, which 'trap' puts in MUST.
explanation.definitionFit: A North American rodent that lives in water and marshes.

clue.text: Fly all over horse

indicators.note: turned over means reversed, so the whole run reads backwards

parts.note: a gnat is a small fly
sum means total, all

explanation.surface: Flies swarm all over a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: GNAT + SUM reversed by 'over' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild horse of the American plains.

clue.text: Pan winter sport Archer's backing

parts.note: skiing is a winter sport

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the archer's name is reversed

parts.note: William Tell was the legendary Swiss archer

explanation.surface: A pan winter sport, with the backing of an archer.
explanation.definitionFit: A skillet is a frying pan.

clue.text: The bird you heard follows me around

indicators.note: follows places one piece after the other
turned around means reversed
heard signals a word said aloud and replaced by its sound

parts.note: you said aloud is the letter U

explanation.surface: A bird is heard to follow me around.
explanation.definitionFit: The emu is a large flightless bird of Australia.

clue.text: Who would find fault with a very hot day?

explanation.definitionFit: To roast is to criticise harshly, and a sweltering day is informally a scorcher of this name.

clue.text: Take-off'll be reported; one's bowled over

indicators.note: reported speech is speech said aloud, so the sound gives the letters

parts.note: a take-off is a skit, a send-up; skit'll is skit will

explanation.surface: An impersonation will be reported; someone is knocked down.
explanation.walkthrough: A skittle is a pin knocked over in the bowling game of skittles.
explanation.definitionFit: A skittle is a wooden pin that a bowled ball knocks over.

clue.text: Tuesday — dry one altogether

parts.note: TT means teetotal, dry
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Tuesday is one dry day all round.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutti is the musical direction for all players together.

clue.text: Murderer crossed river by heap of stones

indicators.note: crossed means passed through, so the river goes inside

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis

explanation.surface: A murderer crossed a river near a pile of stones.
explanation.definitionFit: A cairn is a mound of stones built as a landmark or memorial.

clue.text: Cat trails groggy composer

indicators.note: groggy means unsteady, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A cat follows a dazed musician.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlatti was an Italian Baroque composer.

clue.text: Seasonal electricity charges

parts.note: reads as a utility bill, but means electrical discharges in the warm season

explanation.definitionFit: Sheet lightning seen on warm evenings is the summer form of electrical discharge.
